t: Darwin's five-year voyage on HMS Beagle, from 1831 to 1836, made his name as a geologist and gave him the fossils, finches, mockingbirds and tortoises that puzzled him into asking how species arise.
He devised the theory of natural selection in 1838 but published it only after Alfred Russel Wallace sent him the same idea in 1858; On the Origin of Species followed in 1859.
Evolution was widely accepted by the 1870s, but natural selection as its main mechanism won broad agreement only with the modern evolutionary synthesis of the 1930s to 1950s.
dyk: Seeing a Madagascar orchid with a sixteen-inch nectary, Darwin predicted a moth with a proboscis long enough to pollinate it; explorers found it, Xanthopan, in 1903.
ev: Darwin sails on HMS Beagle as a self-funded naturalist on a survey voyage that lasts almost five years
After reading Malthus on population, Darwin conceives the theory of natural selection
Darwin marries his cousin Emma Wedgwood, is elected a Fellow of the Royal Society and publishes his Beagle Journal
The Structure and Distribution of Coral Reefs appears, and the family moves to Down House in Kent
Darwin's and Wallace's papers on natural selection are presented together at the Linnean Society
On the Origin of Species is published, and its first printing is oversubscribed
The Descent of Man sets out the evidence that humans descend from earlier animals
Darwin dies at Down House and is buried in Westminster Abbey

f.born: 12 February 1809, at The Mount, Shrewsbury, Shropshire; fifth of six children of the doctor and financier Robert Darwin and Susannah Darwin (née Wedgwood)
f.died: 19 April 1882, at Down House, Kent, aged 73, of what his physicians called anginal attacks and heart failure; buried in Westminster Abbey
f.role: Naturalist on HMS Beagle (1831–1836); Secretary of the Geological Society (from 1838); Fellow of the Royal Society (1839); self-funded gentleman scientist at Down House (from 1842)
f.known: the voyage of HMS Beagle; the theory of evolution by natural selection, presented with Alfred Russel Wallace in 1858; On the Origin of Species (1859); The Descent of Man (1871); The Expression of the Emotions (1872); studies of coral reefs, barnacles, orchids and earthworms
